title: Comparatives: -er and more + adjective
grammarNote: Сравнительная степень используется для сравнения ДВУХ вещей, людей или мест. Главное правило: КОРОТКИЕ прилагательные (1-2 слога) → + er. ДЛИННЫЕ прилагательные (3+ слога) → more + прилагательное. После сравнительной степени всегда стоит "than". Есть также неправильные формы, которые нужно запомнить.

grammarTable.subject: Short (1 syllable)
grammarTable.example: Almaty is larger than Uralsk. · It's colder here.

grammarTable.subject: Ends in -e
grammarTable.example: This flat is nicer than the last one.

grammarTable.subject: CVC: double + er
grammarTable.example: My bag is bigger. · The room is hotter in summer.

grammarTable.subject: Ends in -y: y → ier
grammarTable.example: Flat B is noisier than Flat A. · This street is busier.

grammarTable.subject: Long (2+ syllables)
grammarTable.example: This building is more modern than that one.

grammarTable.subject: Irregular
grammarTable.example: good → better · bad → worse · far → further/farther

rows.example: tall → taller · fast → faster · clean → cleaner · dark → darker
nice → nicer · large → larger · close → closer · safe → safer
big → bigger · hot → hotter · thin → thinner · fit → fitter
noisy → noisier · busy → busier · easy → easier · heavy → heavier
modern → more modern · useful → more useful · careful → more careful
expensive → more expensive · important → more important · reliable → more reliable
happy → happier · friendly → friendlier · lovely → lovelier
WKU's teaching is better than at larger universities.
The weather in Astana is worse than in Almaty.
Flat B is further from the university than Flat A.
Uralsk has less traffic than Almaty.
Almaty has more cafés than any other city.
"Flat A is much closer." / "Almaty is far larger than Uralsk."
"Flat B is a bit cheaper." / "This room is slightly darker."
"Astana is even colder in winter." (emphasises surprise)
"Is it as bright as Flat B?" = equal comparison

grammarTip:
Три правила, которые решают 90% случаев:
① 1 слог → + er: tall → taller, big → bigger (CVC!)
② 2+ слога → more + прил: beautiful → more beautiful
③ Исключения: good → better, bad → worse, far → further

❗ НИКОГДА не используй оба варианта вместе: ✗ 'more better', ✗ 'more bigger'!

💡 После сравнительной степени всегда 'than': bigger THAN, more expensive THAN.

Интенсификаторы: much/far (большая разница) / a bit/slightly (маленькая разница).

exercises.hint: "large" ends in -e → add -r: larger. "Almaty is larger than Uralsk." ✅

exercises.text: Flat B is ___ (noisy) than Flat A.
exercises.hint: "noisy" ends in -y → drop y + ier: noisier. "Flat B is noisier." ✅

exercises.text: This professor is ___ (helpful) than the other one.
exercises.hint: "helpful" = 2 syllables → more helpful. Long adjectives use "more".

exercises.text: "This is more better than before" is correct English.
exercises.hint: ✅ "This is better than before." — "good → better" is already irregular. NEVER "more better"!

exercises.text: The weather in Astana is ___ (bad) than in Almaty.
exercises.hint: "bad → worse" (irregular). "The weather is worse in Astana." ✅

exercises.instruction: Which intensifier shows a BIG difference?
exercises.text: Flat A is ___ closer to the university than Flat B.
exercises.hint: "much + comparative" = big difference. "Much closer." ("a bit" = small difference, "very" doesn't go with comparatives)

exercises.text: This room is ___ (hot) than the other one.
Is this university ___ good ___ the one in Almaty?
exercises.hint: "as + adjective + as" = equal comparison. "Is it AS GOOD AS...?" ✅

exercises.text: The journey to Flat B is ___ (far) than to Flat A.
Uralsk has ___ (friendly) people than big cities.
exercises.hint: "friendly" ends in -y → drop y + ier: friendlier. (2-syllable -y words use -ier, not "more")

opts: Almaty is more bigger than Uralsk.
Almaty is the bigger than Uralsk.
exercises.hint: "big → bigger" (CVC, double g). No "more", no "the", always "than". ✅

exercises.text: The teaching here is ___ (good) than at the larger university.

questions.hint: "far → further/farther" (irregular). "further" is more common in British English.
"noisy" ends in -y → drop y + ier: noisier. ✅ (-y words use -ier)

questions.text: "She is more taller than me" is correct.
questions.hint: ✅ "She is taller than me." — NEVER "more" + short adjective. ✗ "more taller"!
"much + comparative" = big difference. "Uralsk is much quieter than Almaty." ✅

questions.text: "Is this flat ___ large ___ the other?" (equal comparison)
questions.hint: "as + adj + as" = equal comparison. "Is it AS LARGE AS the other?" ✅

questions.text: "The canteen food here is ___ (good) than at my previous university."
questions.hint: "good → better" (irregular). The most common irregular comparative.
"more bigger" = ✗ DOUBLE comparative. Never use "more" with short adjective comparatives.
"happy" ends in -y → drop y + ier: happier. ✅ (2-syllable -y words use -ier)

questions.text: "The flat is ___ (large) but ___ (expensive) than I expected."
questions.hint: "large" → larger (-e + r). "expensive" → more expensive (long adj). Both use "than".

opts: surprise at how big the difference is
questions.correct: surprise at how big the difference is
questions.hint: "even colder" = emphasises surprise. "I knew it was cold, but it's EVEN colder than I thought!"
